evidence.description: Clean main source revision used for this review.
The local PostgreSQL adapter connects to a supplied URL, discovers readable resources/schema, enforces explicit selected columns, and reads selected supported values; it does not discover hosts.
CLI draft storage preserves baselines and produces field-level before/after diffs.
CLI patch commands prepare updates and perform point-in-time schema, snapshot, field, type, and relation validation.
CLI source supports scoped-token pairing and revalidated frozen proposal submission.
Server use cases store immutable proposal revisions and require a human reviewer decision on the exact revision.
The browser source presents before/after values and restricts approve/reject controls to a human with review permission.

Architecture documentation records that local sync/execution is not implemented, approval does not apply content, selected snapshots/schema metadata leave the client while database credentials are not intentionally submitted, and legacy apply is a separate path.
The root package manifest is private.
The CLI package manifest is private.
No product tests were executed during initial marketing content drafting.
No remote CI run was executed or inspected for initial marketing content drafting.

claims.text: At source revision 4fdbf2c, PatchCTL supports local PostgreSQL resource/schema discovery from a supplied connection, explicit selected columns, and selected-value reads.
The inspected source supports local drafts, diffs, and point-in-time validation.
The inspected source supports scoped-token pairing, immutable proposal submission, and browser human approval of the exact revision.
Local sync/execution is not implemented, and browser approval does not apply content.
Database URL/password are not intentionally submitted, but selected snapshots and schema metadata leave the client for review.
Legacy server-connected apply is separate and does not establish local-sync support.
The root and CLI packages are private.
No product tests or remote CI were run for this initial draft, and it is not a release, deployment, or adoption claim.
